column8: Iku (to go) → itte, the irregular te-form. Here it links “go straight” to the following instruction; it is not past tense.

column1: Futatsume no kado o hidari ni magatte kudasai.
column2: Turn left at the second corner.
column3: 二つ目の角を左に曲がってください
column5:
すみません、本屋はどこですか？
Sumimasen, honya wa doko desu ka?
Excuse me, where is the bookstore? — Answer segment 2 of 3
column6: 二つ目|の|角|を|左|に|曲がって|ください
column8: Magaru (u-verb, to turn) → magatte + kudasai = please turn. Futatsume means second.

column1: Honya wa michi no hidarigawa ni arimasu yo.
column2: The bookstore is on the left side of the street.
column3: 本屋は道の左側にありますよ
column5:
すみません、本屋はどこですか？
Sumimasen, honya wa doko desu ka?
Excuse me, where is the bookstore? — Answer segment 3 of 3
column6: 本屋|は|道|の|左側|に|あります|よ
column8: Aru (u-verb, to exist) → arimasu, polite nonpast. Use aru for a place or inanimate thing, not iru.
